Mayson.summary: Present on all 12 active accounts and the single busiest ALTR voice this week, but the shape of the work is the problem: 44 reminders and 40 overdue commitments against zero commitments closed. The recurring failure is the offer that never lands — a call proposed, accepted by the client, then never scheduled. It happened to Lauryn (she replied in ten minutes and picked the day; no link ever came), Shayna (fourth month slipped, dropped after she said yes), Lauren Blake (call request ignored by a client who used to answer same-day), Vale (first unanswered call request in six months) and Amber Haze — where a third call offer in eighteen days was the last thing said to her before she terminated 86 minutes later. He also wrote the final words ALTR will ever send Alex Paige Moore: a two-word thanks for her closing payment.
strengths: Only ALTR person proactively working several accounts — when he goes quiet the chat goes quiet entirely (Sarah: his first fully absent window, and ALTR's total output fell to three messages).

Recovered a blocked custom brief on Lauryn by re-typing the ask into the chat body 18 minutes after she said four times the Google Sheets link would not render on her device — the client engaged immediately. This is a reusable fix, not a one-off.
coaching_flags: Offers calls instead of answers. Three call offers in 18 days to Amber Haze produced zero written outcomes and the third ended the engagement. A results question needs a written result, not a meeting.

Proposes calls he does not then schedule: Lauryn, Shayna, Lauren Blake, Vale and Liza Kovalenko all accepted or were offered a call this window that was never booked. Every prior call on these accounts had a link in the thread on the day.
Opens asks faster than he closes them — five simultaneously open requests on Alanna, none ever asked a third time; four workstreams opened on Sarah in three weeks then abandoned.
Re-asks clients for things they have already supplied or already refused (Shayna's credentials across 8/28, 9/9, 9/16; Alanna's Drive uploads after she declined on 9/10).

Stephski.summary: Across all 12 accounts, and the pattern reversed hard this week: collection remained efficient while reconciliation stopped almost entirely. Clients paid — Lilia in full three days early, Lauryn inside term for the first time since December, Alex Paige Moore's $5,259.90 closing balance in 33 hours, Barbara's $1,683.12 correction — and almost none of it was confirmed back with a number. Liza's $10,000 has been unconfirmed for nine days after an explicit promise to report when it cleared; Vale has three consecutive unreconciled transfers; Sarah Lloyd's due date passed in silence on an account rail nobody has verified can receive her wire. Amber Haze asked for her own final invoice and offered to pay immediately — four days later it has not been sent.
strengths: Collection works: four full balances collected this window with no disputes, including a churned client's closing invoice inside 33 hours.
Honoured the soft-chase instruction on Lauryn — one message framed around the client's own deadline rather than a service-pause threat.
coaching_flags: Acknowledges payments without stating an amount — five consecutive times on Lauryn ('thank you love!!'), and no invoice figure has appeared in Lilia's chat in four months. Clients cannot verify what they owe.
Broke an explicit payment commitment and went silent (Liza: 'Its currently in processing on hold ill let you know when it clears', then nine days of nothing on $10,000).

Chases on the deadline while the client's service is broken — Barbara was sent a day-six pause-of-work countdown while her main account was banned and every service question sat unanswered. Last week's report asked specifically for this not to happen.

Banking-detail churn is now a standing risk: five changes in twelve months on Alex Paige Moore, four in six weeks on Barbara, an unverified renamed account on Sarah Lloyd, and a 'bounce backs' admission on Vale's own invoice that is 10 days unexplained.

Last week's reports set two consecutive misses as the explicit red line; that line has now been crossed on ten accounts at once. This is the one service several clients thanked ALTR for every single week, and on Barbara and Lauren Blake they have now stopped asking about it.
strengths: The cadence she built was genuinely the best-delivered service in the agency — eleven and twelve week unbroken runs, client-acknowledged every time. The asset is the reason the outage is this expensive.
